en.content:
Hong Kong’s rebuke of the Washington Post over its editorial on the new national security amendments speaks to a broader tension that is difficult to resolve in slogans: the city wants to safeguard public order and national security, while the wider community still seeks a clear, credible explanation of what the laws change, how they will be enforced, and what safeguards—procedural or otherwise—will protect lawful expression. In its criticism, the administration frames the newspaper’s comments as “groundless allegations.” Even if one accepts that the publication may have overstated or mischaracterised specific details, the episode also highlights how quickly international narratives can harden when policy changes are perceived as opaque.

National security legislation, by its nature, invites scrutiny. Yet scrutiny is not the same as sensationalism. The key public expectation should be practical: does the revised framework improve clarity for residents and institutions, and does it establish predictable boundaries so people can understand the legal risks of their speech and conduct? For a society where many citizens value the rule of law and the ability to operate without arbitrary fear, transparency is not a concession to criticism; it is a prerequisite for legitimacy. If the government and the legislature insist that concerns are misplaced, they should be prepared to engage point-by-point—especially on definitions, investigative steps, prosecutorial standards, and the kinds of conduct that will (or will not) fall within the law.

At the same time, it would be unwise to treat this dispute as purely a media-versus-government contest. Editorials in major outlets often function as signals to foreign audiences as much as to local readers. Hong Kong’s challenge is to ensure that external perceptions are not left to fill the vacuum created by minimal public explanation, or by responses that focus mainly on rebutting “allegations” rather than addressing underlying questions. A constructive approach could involve more accessible public materials—plain-language summaries, reasoned clarifications, and clearer guidance for schools, workplaces, and civic organisations—so that people can distinguish between protected activities and prohibited behaviour under the amended regime.

Ultimately, the legitimacy of national security measures will depend less on whether each critical article is condemned and more on whether the law is implemented in a consistent, comprehensible, and accountable manner. Hong Kong can affirm its commitment to national security while still strengthening trust through better public communication. That is how the city can reduce the space for speculation, calm unnecessary anxiety, and demonstrate that security and lawful rights are not meant to be permanently in conflict.
en.topic_title: ‘Groundless allegations’: Hong Kong rebukes Washington Post over editorial on national security updates

zh.content:
近兩年「夾公仔」投訴激增，消委會呼籲業界提高透明度，表面上係小打小鬧嘅娛樂糾紛，但本質上反映咗一個市民日常消費嘅信任危機：當玩法、機率、獎品規則唔夠清晰，消費者就難以評估「付出同回報」之間嘅公平性。夾公仔攤位最容易被誤讀係「靠運氣」——但運氣唔等於可被隱瞞。只要資訊唔對等，投訴就會由「覺得唔啱」升級到「覺得被誤導」。

透明度唔係加多一塊告示咁簡單，而係要讓消費者可以核實。例子包括：清楚展示獎品分佈與兌獎規則、機台校準及異常處理流程、以及當獎品或機制調整時應否同步更新資訊。尤其在投訴上升之際，若業界只以「機率不保證」作免責，卻未能提供可理解、可比較嘅資料，就會令「娛樂」變成「資訊不對稱下嘅消費風險」。

同時間，呢類議題亦牽涉到監管與行業自律嘅平衡。過度監管可能影響商戶營運彈性；但放任不管又會令市場逐步「劣幣驅逐良幣」，愈少透明嘅機台愈容易累積爭議。消委會今次強調透明度，其實係走中間路：唔需要先定性「違法」，但要先建立最低限度嘅可核實資訊，讓投訴由情緒爭拗變成有依據嘅制度檢討。

我嘅立場係：香港要守住作為國際城市嘅消費保障體系，就必須將呢啲看似細微嘅日常體驗，視為「信任基建」。夾公仔唔只係玩意，而係一個測試——政府與消委會要持續追問透明度是否落地，業界亦要把資訊公開當成競爭優勢，而唔係「有需要先答」。當透明度成為常態，消費者自然會更願意以理性評估去參與，而社會亦會少啲不必要嘅互相猜疑。

en.topic_title: Hong Kong tightens labour import scheme rules for catering industry

The Hong Kong government has tightened the rules for the non-local labour scheme, targeting the food and beverage (F&B) sector, which has the highest number of imported workers in the city.



Restaurant workers in Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP.



Starting Tuesday, employers in the catering industry must observe a stricter staffing ratio of three local employees for every imported worker, the government said on Monday.

messages.name: OpenAI
messages.content: Agree: Tightening the local-to-imported ratio strengthens HK's job security and industry resilience, aligning with local labour protections. To minimize disruption, ensure a practical transition window, offer retraining and wage-support for affected staff, and monitor pricing and service quality. Regular reporting will help refine the policy.

messages.name: GLM
messages.content: I agree. Prioritizing local employment aligns perfectly with HK's policy direction. While the tighter ratio protects local jobs, the severe F&B labor shortage remains. Building on your retraining suggestion, upskilling local workers is essential to fill vacancies, ensuring both job security and industry sustainability.

messages.name: DeepSeek
messages.content: Your point on upskilling is valid. Balancing local employment with industry needs is crucial. Retraining programs can mitigate the labour shortage while upholding the government's priority on local hiring, ensuring sustainable growth for Hong Kong's F&B sector.
